the following questions:

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
securities lending is a source of funding, and that it is a source of wholesale (or long-term) funding.
securities lending is a source of wholesale financing for insurers, and that this financing is used to fund long-dated assets.

the securities lending program is a source of short-term funding for life insurance companies, but that the program is used for a variety of reasons, and not necessarily to finance the purchase of short-term assets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
securities lending is an alternative source of wholesale funding that is more prevalent among life insurers than previously thought.

securities lending programs can be used by life insurers to finance a portfolio consisting of long-dated bonds and that this strategy is not only feasible but has become a popular one in the industry.
securities lending as a wholesale funding mechanism is an important but understudied phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existing literature has not fully accounted for the potential impact that securities lending programs may have on market liquidity.
securities lending programs can serve as a source of funding for life insurers’ long-dated portfolios and can potentially be an important factor for the stability of the U.S. securities market.
securities lending programs should be viewed as a wholesale funding source, rather than a source of liquidity, by both regulators and the market.
